scope: New Latvian source-checked problem-solving article for Christmas/Thanksgiving cactus flowering, bud drop and autumn/winter care; identification comparison includes Easter cactus.

reviewedSources.usedFor: Rest periods, watering without full desiccation, summer location, minimum temperature and conditional repotting.
Hybrid identification limitations, uninterrupted long nights and interaction with temperature; distinct Easter cactus flowering sequence.
Several weeks of short days, cool night temperatures, bud drop, overwatering/root-rot signs and occasional natural bud shedding.
Daylength/temperature interaction, checking pot moisture and drainage, avoiding standing water.
Commercial flowering schedules may not repeat at home; repot only when needed, after-flowering care and desiccated root caution.
Pointed stem segments, autumn/winter flowering, light/temperature stress, photo attribution.
Hybrid identity, rounded segment margins, pendulous flowers, bud-drop causes, photo attribution.
Easter cactus names, star-shaped flowers, spring season, photo attribution.

editorialDecisions: No guarantee of flowering on Christmas Day. Distinguishes bud formation from maintaining already formed buds.
Photoperiod response varies with cultivar and temperature. About six weeks and 14–16 hours darkness are a practical starting point, not an exact universal timer.
Avoided 4 °C flowering-induction advice appearing on the NC State truncata page; RHS recommends keeping these tender plants above 10 °C.
No fixed weekly watering interval, complete drought prescription, fertilizer cure, calendar-only repotting or generic all-cactus treatment.
Does not equate every wilted plant with underwatering or diagnose a pathogen solely from appearance.
Both NC State and extension sources have different Easter cactus nomenclature; article supplies commonly encountered synonyms without claiming a separate plant family.
No recipes involving pesticides or household chemicals. No pet toxicity digression.
No claim that the topic has measured Latvian Google Trends growth. This is a seasonal editorial addition.

imageReview.method: Per-image author/license checked on source plant pages; downloaded source files inspected visually; selected full frames converted to WebP with sharp quality 86, no crop or enlargement.
